Cookie Policy

Last updated: July 7, 2026

This Cookie Policy explains how iD! Training & Development uses cookies and similar technologies on its website, customer portal, checkout, digital-product, download, training, and examination pages.

This policy should be read together with our Privacy Policy, which explains how we collect, use, store, and protect personal data.

1. Who is responsible for cookies

The website and Services are operated by:

iD! Training & Development

2. What cookies and similar technologies are

Cookies are small text files that a website stores on your browser or device. They can contain an identifier or limited information that allows the website to recognise a browser, maintain a session, remember a preference, or provide a particular function.

We may also use similar technologies, including:

  • browser local storage or session storage;
  • security and antiforgery tokens;
  • software-development-kit identifiers;
  • scripts and tags;
  • server-side session identifiers; and
  • security technologies used to detect automated or malicious activity.

In this policy, we use the term "cookies" to refer collectively to cookies and these similar technologies where appropriate.

3. Cookie categories

3.1 Strictly necessary cookies

Strictly necessary cookies are required to operate the website or provide a feature that you expressly request. They may be used to:

  • keep you signed in;
  • maintain an authenticated portal session;
  • protect forms against cross-site request-forgery attacks;
  • apply security and access controls;
  • remember cookie-consent choices;
  • maintain checkout and payment workflows;
  • route requests securely and reliably;
  • prevent fraud, abuse, and automated attacks; and
  • provide other core functions that you request.

These cookies may normally be used without your consent because the website or requested service cannot function properly without them. We still provide information about them through this Cookie Policy.

3.2 Preference cookies

Preference cookies remember choices that change how the website behaves or appears, such as:

  • your selected language or culture;
  • display or interface preferences;
  • previously selected portal options; and
  • other settings that you ask the website to remember.

Some preference cookies may be strictly necessary for a feature that you have expressly requested. Other preference cookies will be used only where permitted by law or after obtaining consent where required.

3.3 Analytics cookies

We do not currently intend to use optional analytics cookies unless an analytics service is separately enabled.

If analytics are enabled, they may be used to understand matters such as:

  • which pages are visited;
  • how users navigate through the website;
  • which features are used;
  • whether errors occur; and
  • how website performance and usability can be improved.

Limited analytics cookies that have little or no impact on privacy may, where legally permitted, be used without consent. Analytics that track identifiable behaviour or have more than a minor privacy impact will be activated only after valid consent has been obtained.

3.4 Marketing and tracking cookies

We do not currently intend to use advertising or cross-site tracking cookies unless marketing functionality is separately enabled.

Marketing or tracking cookies may be used to:

  • measure advertising campaigns;
  • build or supplement advertising profiles;
  • personalise advertisements;
  • track users across websites or services; or
  • connect website activity to advertising or social-media platforms.

These cookies will not be placed or accessed before you have given valid consent where consent is required.

3.5 Embedded-content cookies

Pages may contain content supplied by an external provider, such as a video, map, scheduling tool, social-media component, payment feature, or another embedded service.

An external provider may place cookies or receive technical information when its content is loaded. Where the embedded feature is optional and requires consent, it will not be loaded until the required consent has been obtained.

4. Cookies and technologies used by the platform

The exact cookie name may differ between environments or change following a technical update. The following table describes the cookies and technologies that the platform may use.

Cookie or technology Provider Purpose Category Typical duration
ASP.NET Core Identity authentication cookie iD! Training & Development Authenticates your account, keeps you signed in, and applies account and role-based permissions. Strictly necessary Session-based or for the configured sign-in period. A longer duration may apply if a "remember me" option is selected.
ASP.NET Core antiforgery cookie iD! Training & Development Protects forms and authenticated requests against cross-site request-forgery attacks. Strictly necessary Normally for the browser session or until the token expires.
Session or temporary workflow cookie iD! Training & Development Maintains temporary state required for portal, form, examination, checkout, upload, or account workflows. Strictly necessary Normally until the browser session ends or the temporary workflow expires.
Language or culture cookie iD! Training & Development Remembers your selected website language and regional culture. Preference Until its configured expiry date or until you delete it.
Cookie-consent preference iD! Training & Development Records whether you accepted or rejected optional cookie categories and prevents the consent notice from being shown unnecessarily. Strictly necessary Normally up to 12 months, unless your choice is renewed or changed sooner.
Cloudflare security and network technologies Cloudflare Helps deliver website traffic, protect the website, detect malicious or automated requests, and maintain network availability. Strictly necessary Varies depending on the security or network feature used.
Cloudflare Turnstile Cloudflare Helps distinguish legitimate users from automated or abusive activity on protected forms or workflows. Used only on pages where Turnstile is enabled. Strictly necessary where enabled to protect the relevant form Temporary security information may be retained for the period necessary to complete and validate the challenge.
Stripe checkout and payment technologies Stripe Processes payments, maintains checkout security, prevents fraud, and completes payment redirects. Strictly necessary for payment workflows Determined by Stripe according to the relevant payment and security purpose.

Cookies shown in your browser may use technical names beginning with prefixes such as .AspNetCore.. Automatically generated suffixes may differ between development, staging, and production environments.

5. Local storage and session storage

The website may use browser local storage or session storage for limited interface, workflow, or application state. Unlike a traditional cookie, this information is stored within your browser and is not automatically sent with every request.

Session storage is normally deleted when the relevant browser tab or session ends. Local-storage information remains until it is deleted by the application, expires under the applicable logic, or is cleared through your browser.

We will not use local storage to bypass a refusal of optional cookies or to perform tracking that would otherwise require consent.

6. Legal basis and consent

Strictly necessary cookies are used because they are required to provide the website or a service that you have expressly requested, or because they are reasonably necessary for security, fraud prevention, and the reliable operation of the Services.

Where a cookie or similar technology is not strictly necessary and consent is required, we will ask for consent before activating it.

Consent must be freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous. Rejecting optional cookies must be reasonably as easy as accepting them. Optional categories will not be enabled through preselected choices.

Refusing optional cookies will not prevent you from accessing the basic website, although an optional feature that depends on a particular provider may remain unavailable.

7. Changing or withdrawing your cookie choices

Where optional cookies are used, you can change or withdraw your consent at any time through the cookie settings made available on the website.

Withdrawing consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing that occurred before consent was withdrawn. After withdrawal, the relevant optional cookies will no longer be used, although existing cookies may need to be removed through the consent tool or your browser settings.

If the website currently uses only strictly necessary cookies, a separate consent banner may not be displayed. This policy will still explain which cookies are used.

8. Browser controls

Most browsers allow you to inspect, block, or delete cookies through their privacy or security settings. Browser controls differ, so consult the help documentation for your browser or device.

Blocking or deleting strictly necessary cookies may cause parts of the Services to stop working. Depending on the cookie affected, you may be unable to:

  • sign in or remain signed in;
  • access protected portal pages;
  • submit forms securely;
  • complete a checkout or payment;
  • upload or download files;
  • take or continue an examination;
  • retain your selected language; or
  • retain your cookie preferences.

9. Third-party providers

Some cookies and similar technologies are operated by external providers. Depending on the features you use, these may include:

  • Cloudflare, for content delivery, network security, object storage, and Turnstile security checks where enabled;
  • Stripe, for checkout, payment processing, and payment-fraud prevention;
  • hosting, email, monitoring, or analytics providers where such services are enabled; and
  • providers of optional embedded content where such content is included on a page.

Third-party providers may process technical information under their own privacy notices and cookie policies. Their retention periods and cookie names may change independently from ours.

A link to an external website or social-media profile does not by itself place that provider's cookies through our website. Cookies may be placed after you follow the link and visit the provider's own service.

10. Analytics and marketing services added later

If we introduce an analytics, advertising, social-media, or other optional technology, we will update this Cookie Policy and, where required:

  • identify the provider and purpose;
  • describe the types of information collected;
  • state the applicable cookie duration;
  • prevent the technology from loading before consent;
  • provide an equally accessible reject option; and
  • allow consent to be withdrawn later.

We will not treat continued browsing, silence, inactivity, or a preselected option as consent where valid consent is legally required.

11. Changes to this Cookie Policy

We may update this Cookie Policy when our website, cookie usage, providers, security measures, or legal obligations change.

The current version will be published on this page and identified by the "Last updated" date. Where a change materially affects an optional technology for which consent is required, we may ask you to make a new choice.

12. Contact

For questions about this Cookie Policy or the use of cookies, contact:
